changes.comment: Three new MCP tools let a caller follow one Feishu document's comments: `subscribe_document`, `unsubscribe_document`, and `list_subscriptions`. Each is offered to both the Dispatcher and a TeamLeader with no recipient argument — the caller is the recipient — so a caller can only create, list, and remove its own rows. Subscribing takes a document URL or a token plus its `type`, resolves a wiki URL to the document the node holds, and refuses when Feishu proves this bot cannot see the document. Subscriptions live in a third `subscriptions` section of the channel's existing routing document, which stays readable as it is: a file written before this release reads the section as empty. A received comment event produces one submission per subscriber, carrying the comment's identifying facts, what the commenter wrote, and the document text it is anchored to, and pointing at lark-cli for the rest of the thread; the text is read once per delivered event and its absence never costs the event; a comment nobody subscribed to reaches the Dispatcher Agent when it @-mentions the bot and the commenter is already one of the dispatcher's trusted users, and is dropped and logged otherwise — that delivery creates no subscription. A subscriber whose Team is closed or gone loses its own subscription and no one else's, and dissolving a Team drops its subscriptions alongside its bindings. Feishu delivers these events only when the bot itself would be notified — the comment or reply @-mentions the bot, or the reply lands in a thread the bot has already replied in.
